Анна сказала Марии, что она победила.

сказала

победила

CONTENT_LINK: CHILD is semantic content or selected complement of PARENT: what is said, known, wanted, decided, requested, begun, etc. If CHILD is what PARENT wants/decides/requests/begins, use CONTENT_LINK even though CHILD is intended.
GOAL_LINK: CHILD is an adjunct goal for which PARENT itself is performed: 'PARENT in order to CHILD'. Do not use GOAL_LINK for wanted/decided/requested/begun content.
CAUSE_LINK: CHILD is the reason/cause that explains why PARENT happens.
TIME_LINK: CHILD locates PARENT in time or supplies the temporal situation relative to which PARENT occurs.
PLACE_LINK: CHILD supplies the place/location in relation to which PARENT occurs.
SOURCE_LINK: CHILD is the source/origin situation from which PARENT or its content arises.
MANNER_LINK: CHILD describes the manner/procedure by which PARENT is carried out.
SEPARATE: CHILD is structurally nearby/dependent but fills none of the listed semantic relations of PARENT.
QUESTION:
Which one relation best describes CHILD relative to PARENT? First distinguish selected CONTENT from adjunct PURPOSE: if CHILD is what PARENT means/wants/decides/requests/begins, choose CONTENT_LINK; choose GOAL_LINK only when PARENT itself is done in order to achieve CHILD. Then compare the remaining listed meanings.
CHOICES:
CONTENT_LINK
GOAL_LINK
CAUSE_LINK
TIME_LINK
PLACE_LINK
SOURCE_LINK
MANNER_LINK
SEPARATE

Choose exactly one label from CHOICES. CONTENT_LINK = selected content/complement: what is said, known, wanted, decided, requested, begun. If CHILD is what PARENT wants/decides/requests/begins, use CONTENT_LINK. GOAL_LINK = PARENT itself is done in order to achieve CHILD. Surface form is evidence only. Return only the label.
